pattern: A lane measures a win against a baseline that a CONCURRENT lane then invalidates. The number was true when taken and is false by the time it is read. Parallel fan-out causes this structurally - it is the cost of the throughput.

the_rule: A lane result is valid only against the HEAD it was measured on. Before merging any lane that branched before a landed change to the same files: check ancestry, rebase, RE-MEASURE. Do not merge a number whose baseline no longer exists.
cheap_check: git merge-base --is-ancestor <landed-commit> <lane-branch> - if NO, the lane predates it and its baseline is suspect wherever the files overlap.
why_this_is_not_an_argument_against_fan_: All three were caught, two of them BY the fan-out itself: the diagnosis lane found the simd subsumption, and the descent lane flagged its own transferred assumption. The fix is an ancestry check at merge time, not fewer lanes.
